newsitem.title: GERMANY: Latam soya output crucial for 1997 world demand.
newsitem.headline: Latam soya output crucial for 1997 world demand.

text.p: Latin American soybean output needed to be strong in early 1997 to satisfy world demand due to less sunflowerseed and rapeseed available, the independent newsletter Oil World said on Tuesday.
Demand for sunseed and rapeseed was firm, especially in Europe, but sunseed production in the 1996/97 season was seen 1.1 million tonnes lower at 24.7 million, it said.

Global sunseed crushings were likely to rise by 400,000 tonnes to 8.4 million tonnes in the September/December period from a year ago. But crushing activity would slow in the second half of the 96/97 (Oct/Sept) season.
Combined world sunseed and rapeseed stocks on January 1, 1997 were forecast down 13 percent from a year earlier at 3.7 million tonnes.

The 1996 EU-15 rapeseed crop was estimated at 7.18 million tonnes, down by 1.1 million from 1995. The EU recently agreed large exports to Poland as well as some to Japan, Canada and Mexico, despite its domestic crop shortfalls.
This would turn the EU into a net exporter of rapeseed and make it highly dependent on soybean supplies from overseas. --Vera Eckert, Hamburg newsroom, +49-40-41903275
